title: Important: Ethereum Upgrade
subtitle: Action needed from Ethereum Foundation

messages.text:
Subject: URGENT — Action Required for ETH 2.0 Migration
From: team@ethereum-foundation.org

Dear Ethereum user,

As part of the ETH 2.0 network upgrade, all users must migrate their holdings to the new Proof-of-Stake chain before March 31st.

Wallets that have not migrated will lose access to their ETH permanently.

Click below to connect your wallet and migrate your ETH automatically:

🔗 https://ethereum-foundation.org/migrate

This is mandatory for all ETH holders.

choices.revealText: Sensei says: The Ethereum Foundation communicates through ethereum.org and official social media — never by email. Also, ETH 2.0 migration happened automatically. No user action was ever required!

messages.text:
📋 Email Analysis:
• Sender: team@ethereum-foundation.org
• Official domain: ethereum.org
• ❌ 'ethereum-foundation.org' is NOT the official Ethereum domain!
• This domain was registered 5 days ago

📋 Domain Comparison:
• Real: ethereum.org ✅
• Fake: ethereum-foundation.org ❌

The scammer registered a lookalike domain to impersonate the Ethereum Foundation.
💡 Fact: The ETH 2.0 merge happened automatically. No user needed to 'migrate' anything. If you held ETH, it transferred automatically on the real network.

choices.text: Visit the link anyway — just to see

messages.text: 📄 The page displays the Ethereum logo and a professional layout. It looks official but the domain is wrong.

Connect your wallet to begin the migration process. Your ETH will be transferred to the new Proof-of-Stake chain automatically.

⏰ Only 48 hours remaining before the deadline.

🔐 Wallet Connection Request:
Site: ethereum-foundation.org
Permissions: Full access to wallet, sign transactions

⚠️ This site wants full access to your wallet, including the ability to sign transactions on your behalf.

passiveClues: Domain was registered only 5 days ago
ETH 2.0 merge happened automatically — no migration needed
Ethereum Foundation doesn't send emails to individual users
Urgency tactic: fake 'deadline' to force quick action

activeInvestigations.result: Domain 'ethereum-foundation.org' was registered 5 days ago through an anonymous registrar. The real Ethereum Foundation uses 'ethereum.org' exclusively.
The Ethereum Foundation confirmed: They do NOT send migration emails. The Merge to Proof-of-Stake happened automatically in September 2022. No user action was ever needed.
Security researchers have flagged 'ethereum-foundation.org' as a phishing domain. Over 200 users have reported losing funds to this fake migration scam.

howItWorked.text: Scammer sent a mass email impersonating the Ethereum Foundation using a lookalike domain
The email created urgency with a fake migration deadline
The fake website requested full wallet connection with transaction signing permissions
Once connected, a malicious smart contract is signed that transfers all your ETH and tokens to the scammer

redFlags: The sender's domain doesn't match the official organization's domain
Legitimate blockchain upgrades never require you to 'migrate' manually
Urgency and deadlines pressuring immediate action
Requests for full wallet access or transaction signing permissions
Emails claiming to be from a blockchain foundation that doesn't send mass emails
irlProtection: Always verify the sender's email domain matches the official one exactly
Check official channels (Twitter, blog) to confirm any announcements
Blockchain upgrades are automatic — you never need to 'migrate' tokens manually
Never connect your wallet to a site you reached through an email link
When in doubt, go directly to the official website by typing the URL manually
